sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN UPPER LEVEL RIDGE WILL BUILD ACROSS THE WEST TODAY AS ANTICYCLONE OVER THE FOUR CORNERS INTENSIFIES. FURTHER EAST...A SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL PROGRESS EWD FROM THE UPPER/MID MS VALLEY ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES AND OHIO VALLEY REGIONS. WIDESPREAD THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING THIS MORNING ACROSS PARTS OF THE MID AND UPPER MS VALLEY INTO THE OHIO VALLEY...CREATING A COMPLEX SCENARIO FOR LATER SEVERE POTENTIAL.

sections.title: MID/UPPER MS VALLEY TOWARD THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: THE DEVELOPMENT/EVOLUTION OF SEVERE CONVECTION THIS AFTERNOON WILL DEPEND ON ONGOING CONVECTION EARLY THIS MORNING. A WEAKENING STORM COMPLEX IS EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING IN THE VICINITY OF THE MID-MS VALLEY/CNTRL IL BY 12Z THIS MORNING...AND SEVERAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES WILL BE IN PLACE ACROSS THE LOWER OH VALLEY FROM THE PREVIOUS DAYS CONVECTION. A REMNANT MCV ASSOCIATED WITH THIS PRIOR CONVECTION MAY INTERACT WITH THESE OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES BY EARLY AFTERNOON AFTER DESTABILIZATION OCCURS AND AN UPTICK IN STORM DEVELOPMENT IS ANTICIPATED IN THE VICINITY OF SRN IL/SW IND/WRN KY. THIS ENVIRONMENT WILL BE CHARACTERIZED BY DEWPOINTS IN THE 70S WITH MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY. ADDITIONALLY...DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL BE ADEQUATE FOR INITIALLY A FEW SUPERCELLS WHERE GREATEST DESTABILIZATION IS EXPECTED /LOWER OH VALLEY/...BEFORE QUICKLY GROWING UPSCALE INTO AN MCS. ALL SEVERE WEATHER TYPES WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY SUPERCELLS THAT DEVELOP. ONE LIMITING FACTOR MAY BE THE RESULT OF BUILDING WRN RIDGE/NW FLOW REGIME...WITH WARMING TEMPERATURES ALOFT EXPECTED THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. THIS WILL HINDER MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES BUT INSTABILITY/SHEAR PARAMETERS WILL BE SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT VIGOROUS THUND

sections.title: NORTHEAST STATES
sections.text: A WEAK SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL TRACK EWD ACROSS NY/PA AND SRN NEW ENGLAND TODAY. ENHANCED W/SWLY FLOW OVER A WARM/MOIST AIRMASS WILL AID IN THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT BY LATE MORNING/EARLY AFTERNOON...WHERE WEAK DESTABILIZATION OCCURS IN BROKEN CLOUDS. POOR LAPSE RATES WILL GENERALLY LIMIT LARGE HAIL POTENTIAL /MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL STILL POSSIBLE GIVEN COOLER TEMPS ALOFT/...BUT FASTER STORM MOTION AND SOME DRY MIDLEVEL AIR WILL PROMOTE SEVERE WIND POTENTIAL. ..LEITMAN/BROYLES.. 06/26/2013

sections.title: MID MS AND LOWER/MID OH VALLEYS
sections.text: MORNING RADAR AND SATELLITE LOOPS SHOW TWO STRONG MCS/S PERSISTING THIS MORNING OVER IL...ONE SOUTHEAST OF STL AND ONE WEST OF CMI. BOTH OF THESE CLUSTERS OF STORMS HAVE BEEN ONGOING FOR SEVERAL HOURS...ARE ASSOCIATED WITH A MID LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH...AND SHOW CONSIDERABLE MESOSCALE ORGANIZATION. HOWEVER...NEITHER OF THE SYSTEMS HAVE PRODUCED SEVERE WIND GUSTS IN THE LAST SEVERAL HOURS. 12Z RAOBS AT LZK/SGF/ILX/BNA SHOW A LARGE RESERVOIR OF STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND POTENTIAL AFTERNOON CAPE VALUES OVER 2500 J/KG AHEAD OF THE STORMS. THIS SUGGESTS THE RISK OF INTENSIFICATION AFTER A FEW HOURS OF DAYTIME HEATING. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT ONE OR MORE SWATHS OF WIND DAMAGE ARE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORM CLUSTERS...ALTHOUGH SPECIFIC DETAILS OF THEIR EVOLUTION ARE NOT CLEAR AT THIS TIME. THE AREAS THAT SEEM MOST PRONE TO THIS THREAT ARE FROM EASTERN IL ACROSS MUCH OF IND/OH/KY. ..NORTHEAST STATES AND MID ATLANTIC REGION... SIMILAR TO YESTERDAY...POCKETS OF STRONG HEATING WILL LEAD TO MODERATE INSTABILITY FROM SOUTHERN NY AND MUCH OF MA SOUTHWARD INTO VA. MOST MODEL SOLUTIONS SHOW ISOLATED TO SCATTERED AFTERNOON THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT OVER THIS REGION. WESTERLY FLOW ALOFT IS

sections.title: MN/WI INTO LOWER MI
sections.text: AMPLE RESIDUAL LOW LEVEL MOISTURE IS PRESENT FROM MN SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS WI AND NORTHERN IL INTO SOUTHERN LOWER MI. CONSIDERABLE CLOUD COVER IS PRESENT THIS MORNING ALONG THIS CORRIDOR...BUT A FEW BREAKS ARE EXPECTED LATER TODAY AS THE PRIMARY UPPER TROUGH AXIS ROTATES THROUGH THE REGION. VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE WEAK...BUT SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY MAY RESULT IN ISOLATED HAIL/WIND REPORTS DURING THE PEAK HEATING PERIOD. ..HART/ROGERS.. 06/26/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SUBSTANTIAL STRENGTHENING AND EXPANSION OF THE SUBTROPICAL HIGH ...NOW CENTERED OVER SOUTHWEST TEXAS...IS FORECAST THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE PERIOD...WITH A NORTHWARD SHIFT TOWARD THE FOUR CORNERS REGION. AS THIS OCCURS...FURTHER AMPLIFICATION OF UPPER RIDGING IS EXPECTED IN A BROAD ARC...EITHER SIDE OF AN AXIS EXTENDING NORTHWARD THROUGH THE NORTHERN ROCKIES...ALONG THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER. WITHIN STRENGTHENING AND INCREASINGLY NORTHWESTERLY MID/UPPER FLOW DOWNSTREAM OF THIS FEATURE...MODELS INDICATE THAT A SIGNIFICANT SHORT WAVE IMPULSE WILL PROGRESS ACROSS THE NORTHERN PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...WHILE TROUGHING WITH EMBEDDED SMALLER SCALE PERTURBATIONS...NOW OVER THE LOWER OHIO VALLEY...TURNS EASTWARD TOWARD THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS. MEANWHILE...BROADER SCALE TROUGHING WITH EMBEDDED PERTURBATIONS FROM THE LOWER GREAT LAKES THROUGH SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND WILL CONTINUE TO SHIFT EASTWARD TODAY AND TONIGHT...WHILE ANOTHER SIGNIFICANT IMPULSE WITHIN CYCLONIC FLOW ACROSS EASTERN CANADA APPROACHES NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND. STEEPEST MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ASSOCIATED WITH VERY WARM AND STRONGLY CAPPING ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR ARE NOW GENERALLY CONFINED

sections.title: LOWER OHIO/TENNESSEE VALLEYS INTO CENTRAL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: HIGHEST SEVERE PROBABILITIES TODAY APPEAR TO EXIST ACROSS KENTUCKY AND TENNESSEE. THE MOST NOTABLE ONGOING CONVECTION APPEARS TO BE THE CLUSTER NOW DEVELOPING SOUTHEASTWARD OUT OF EAST CENTRAL ILLINOIS TOWARD THE EVANSVILLE/LOUISVILLE AREA. THIS ACTIVITY APPEARS TO BE SUPPORTED BY AN AREA OF SUSTAINED MID-LEVEL FORCING FOR UPWARD MOTION...WITH LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION CONTRIBUTING TO SOUTHWARD DEVELOPMENT...WHILE MID-LEVEL FORCING SHIFTS EASTWARD TOWARD THE APPALACHIANS. WITH FURTHER HEATING AND DESTABILIZATION OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS KENTUCKY/TENNESSEE AND ADJACENT AREAS...THE EVOLUTION OF A LARGE CLUSTER OF STORMS APPEARS POSSIBLE AT SOME POINT THIS AFTERNOON. UNCERTAINTY LINGERS JUST HOW QUICKLY THIS WILL OCCUR...BUT THE EVOLUTION OF AN ORGANIZED MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM CAPABLE OF GENERATING CONSIDERABLE DAMAGING WIND GUSTS APPEARS POSSIBLE. ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO PROPAGATE SOUTHEASTWARD INTO/THROUGH THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS AND TENNESSEE VALLEY BY LATE EVENING. FOR ADDITIONAL NEAR TERM INFORMATION...REFER TO SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1244.

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY
sections.text: CONSIDERABLE UNCERTAINTY CONCERNING CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL LINGERS AS MID/UPPER FLOW TRENDS NORTHWESTERLY LATER TODAY/TONIGHT. GUIDANCE IS SUGGESTIVE OF SCATTERED AREAS OF CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND TONIGHT ACROSS PARTS OF THE DAKOTAS INTO THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY...WHERE AT LEAST SOME DRYING HAS OCCURRED. HOWEVER...HIGHEST CONFIDENCE IN RENEWED STORM DEVELOPMENT STILL APPEARS ACROSS PARTS OF EAST CENTRAL MINNESOTA INTO NORTHERN WISCONSIN TOWARD EARLY EVENING. THE ENVIRONMENT REMAINS QUITE MOIST ACROSS THIS REGION...AND SUPPORTIVE OF LARGE CAPE...WITH INCREASING FORCING FOR LARGE-SCALE ASCENT EXPECTED CLOSE /SHORTLY AFTER/ PEAK BOUNDARY LAYER INSTABILITY.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC COAST STATES INTO NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: A BELT OF MODEST LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC FLOW COULD ENHANCE STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON IN A MOIST UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT EAST OF THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS THROUGH THE NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC AND SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND COAST. MEANWHILE...THE APPROACH OF THE SHORT WAVE TROUGH DIGGING ACROSS QUEBEC COULD CONTRIBUTE TO INCREASING THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY ACROSS PARTS OF UPSTATE NEW YORK INTO NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND. BUT THIS LATTER DEVELOPMENT MAY NOT OCCUR UNTIL AFTER WELL AFTER THE ONSET OF DIURNAL SURFACE COOLING...SO POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE WIND AND HAIL STILL REMAINS UNCLEAR.

sections.title: SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: MODELS SUGGEST THAT A WEAK IMPULSE PIVOTING EASTWARD/SOUTHWARD AROUND THE EASTERN PERIPHERY OF THE DEVELOPING SUBTROPICAL HIGH CENTER COULD PROVIDE FORCING TO SUPPORT STORM DEVELOPMENT WITH THE APPROACH OF CONVECTIVE TEMPERATURES ACROSS THE EASTERN TEXAS PANHANDLE AND ADJACENT SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS. TOO MUCH UNCERTAINTY STILL EXISTS CONCERNING THE MAGNITUDE AND SCALE OF THIS POTENTIAL FOR SLIGHT RISK PROBABILITIES AT THE PRESENT TIME...BUT THE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF A SUBSTANTIVE STORM CLUSTER CAPABLE OF PRODUCING STRONG SURFACE GUSTS...PERHAPS SOME HAIL. ..KERR/COHEN.. 06/26/2013

sections.title: LOWER OH/TN VALLEYS TO THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: NO APPRECIABLE CHANGE TO PREVIOUS OUTLOOK PROBABILITIES OR REASONING. STILL AWAITING UPSCALE GROWTH TO A BROADER MCS BEYOND THE CLUSTER OVER SRN IND. 12Z WRF-NMM/NSSL SUGGEST THIS PROCESS SHOULD HAVE OCCURRED BY NOW WITH BOWING SEGMENTS DEPICTED INTO KY THIS EVENING. PERSISTENT LOW-LEVEL WAA AND PRESENCE OF A STRONGLY BUOYANT DOWNSTREAM AIR MASS AMIDST SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR SHOULD YIELD EVENTUAL GROWTH INTO A VIGOROUS SEWD-MOVING MCS WITH DAMAGING WINDS AS THE PRIMARY THREAT. SEE MCD 1250 FOR FURTHER SHORT-TERM FORECAST INFORMATION.

sections.title: NRN/CNTRL PLAINS AND UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: HAVE MAINTAINED SLIGHT RISK PROBABILITIES FOR A PART OF THE UPPER MS VALLEY AHEAD OF CONVECTION ALONG A DECAYING FRONTAL ZONE. ADDED MARGINAL HAIL PROBABILITIES TO PARTS OF NEB FOR LATE TONIGHT AS A FEW ELEVATED TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM WITHIN A LOW-LEVEL WAA REGIME.

sections.title: MID-ATLANTIC TO NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: ADJUSTED SLIGHT RISK PROBABILITIES TO ALONG AND S OF THE DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE. CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS WILL POSE A PRIMARY RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS. SEE MCD 1248/1249/1251 AND WW 373 FOR ADDITIONAL SHORT-TERM FORECAST INFORMATION.

sections.title: SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: CONVECTION APPEARS TO BE INITIATING OVER THE HIGH TERRAIN OF THE TRANS-PECOS AND ADDITIONAL ISOLATED TSTMS MAY FORM LATER FARTHER N ALONG DRYLINE. SPATIAL THREAT APPEARS TOO LIMITED TO WARRANT A SLIGHT RISK. ..GRAMS.. 06/26/2013 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1126 AM CDT WED JUN 26 2013/

sections.title: ERN OH...WV THROUGH KY AND TN AREAS
sections.text: EXPANSIVE MCS OVER THE OH VALLEY WILL CONTINUE DEVELOPING SEWD NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. STRONGER STORMS WILL PROBABLY BE SUSTAINED INTO THE OVERNIGHT WITHIN WRN HALF OF MCS FROM CNTRL THROUGH WRN KY AND EVENTUALLY INTO MIDDLE TN. HERE A BELT OF STRONGER NWLY WINDS ALOFT AND DEEP SHEAR RESIDE ALONG ERN FRINGE OF THE GREATER INSTABILITY. ALSO INFLOW FROM A WLY LLJ WILL BE MAXIMIZED FROM KY INTO THE TN VALLEY. DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL THE MAIN THREATS.

sections.title: ERN SD...ERN NEB INTO SWRN MN AND NWRN IA
sections.text: ISOLATED STORMS DEVELOPING SEWD WITHIN NWLY FLOW REGIME MAY POSE A MODEST SEVERE THREAT NEXT HOUR OR TWO...BUT SHOULD GRADUALLY DIMINISH AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES. HOWEVER...ADDITIONAL STORMS MAY DEVELOP LATER TONIGHT FROM PARTS OF ERN NEB INTO EXTREME SERN SD AND WRN IA WITHIN DEVELOPING WARM ADVECTION REGIME ON NOSE OF A SWLY LLJ. SOME OF THIS ACTIVITY MAY POSE A MODEST THREAT FOR ISOLATED LARGE HAIL. ..DIAL.. 06/27/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR THREAT MAY INCREASE THROUGH MID-AFTN OVER DISCUSSION AREA...AS EXPANDING AREA OF INITIALLY SUB-SVR CONVECTION OVER SRN IL MOVES INTO INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS AND OBJECTIVE DIAGNOSTICS EACH INDICATE RATHER FRAGMENTED MOISTURE/THERMAL FIELDS ACROSS THIS REGION...RELATED TO PASSAGE OF PRIOR CONVECTION FROM YESTERDAY AND OVERNIGHT. ONE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WAS DRAWN FROM NEAR HTS ACROSS E-CENTRAL KY...TO NEAR SDF...BECOMING MORE DIFFUSE WNWWD ACROSS SERN INDIANA BENEATH RESIDUAL CLOUD/PRECIP COVER OF DECAYING SRN IL/SWRN INDIANA MCS. BOUNDARY IS MOVING NWD 10-15 KT WITH SUBTLE WIND SHIFT AND SFC VORTICITY CORRIDOR STILL EVIDENT. EXPANDING CLUSTER OF TSTMS OVER ERN IL...NEARLY SURROUNDING MTO AS OF 1545Z...IS MOVING ESEWD ALONG AND N OF CURRENT BOUNDARY POSITION AND TOWARD PROGRESSIVELY MORE SUITABLE NEAR-SFC THETAE FOR INTENSIFICATION AND FURTHER EXPANSION WITH DAMAGING GUST RISK. OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL OFFER CONTINUED FOCUS OF AT LEAST SUBTLE LOW-LEVEL LIFT. SFC FLOW IS WEAK NEAR BOUNDARY -- GENERALLY 5-10 KT -- AND HAS BEEN VEERING...WHICH WEAKENS BOTH LOW-LEVEL SHEAR AND STORM-RELATIVE FLOW. HOWEVER...EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR VECTORS -- ENHANCED S OF MCV EVIDENT OVER NERN IL -- BEAR SUBSTANTIAL PARALLEL COMPONENT TO BOUNDARY...WITH MAGNITUDES 35-40 KT IN SUPPORT OF CONVECTIVE ORGANIZATION. PRECONVECTIVE MLCINH HAS BECOME SO WEAK THAT FORCED ASCENT OF RICHLY MOIST AIR MASS...RELATED TO FORWARD PROPAGATION...WOULD BE PLENTY TO MAINTAIN/STRENGTHEN CONVECTION SHOULD COLD POOL GET LARGER AND BETTER ORGANIZED ON STORM SCALE. MEANWHILE DISPERSION/THINNING OF CLOUD COVER WILL PERMIT ENOUGH INSOLATION...IN CONJUNCTION WITH UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S F SFC DEW POINTS...FOR PRECONVECTIVE MLCAPE NEAR 2000 J/KG...BASED ON MODIFIED RAOBS AND ASSORTED MODEL SOUNDINGS. GIVEN THESE CONDITIONS...WW MAY BE REQUIRED IF STORM-MODE TRENDS PROCEED UPSCALE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR AN INCREASING POTENTIAL FOR SVR THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON...AND THE ISSUANCE OF A SVR TSTM WATCH IS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT 7- AND 9-KM RADAR CAPPI DATA INDICATE AN UPTICK IN DEEP CONVECTION ALONG A WEAKLY ORGANIZED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY/DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE ARCING ALONG THE WV/VA BORDER INTO FAR SWRN VA. ADDITIONAL CONVECTION WILL LIKELY DEVELOP INVOF THIS BOUNDARY...AIDED BY DIURNALLY DEEPENING OROGRAPHIC CIRCULATIONS INVOF THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS. THE AIR MASS E OF THE BLUE RIDGE MOUNTAINS IS STRONGLY DESTABILIZING TO THE S OF A MORE W/E-ORIENTED DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE ACROSS S-CENTRAL/SERN PA. DIABATIC SFC HEATING SUPPORTING TEMPERATURES IN THE MIDDLE/UPPER 80S TO AROUND 90 DEGREES AMIDST SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MIDDLE 60S TO AROUND 70F IS SUPPORTING MLCAPE ON THE ORDER OF 1500-3000 J/KG PER MODIFIED 12Z RAOBS. WITH VIS SATELLITE IMAGERY INDICATING PARTLY/MOSTLY SUNNY SKIES AWAY FROM ONGOING CONVECTION...FURTHER DESTABILIZATION IS ANTICIPATED THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. THIS WILL SUPPORT VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS/DOWNDRAFTS...WITH SVR WIND AND HAIL POTENTIAL INCREASING THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AS CONVECTION MOVES OVER THE PIEDMONT AND TOWARD THE COASTAL PLAIN. DCAPE VALUES INCREASING OVER 1000 J/KG AND ENHANCED WATER-LOADING PROCESSES ASSOCIATED WITH PW VALUES OF 1.50-1.75 INCHES PER GPS DATA WILL ENHANCE THE DMGG WIND POTENTIAL. MID-LEVEL FLOW IS ONLY MODEST PER LWX/FCX VWP DATA -- ON THE ORDER OF 20 KT FROM THE W -- WHICH MAY ONLY CONTRIBUTE TO MARGINALLY ORGANIZED...EWD-MOVING MULTICELL STORM CLUSTERS. SOME INCREASE IN MID-LEVEL FLOW/EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR MAY OCCUR LATER TODAY AS A CONVECTIVELY AUGMENTED MID-LEVEL PERTURBATION CURRENTLY OVER OHIO PER MOISTURE CHANNEL IMAGERY APPROACHES. HOWEVER...THIS MAY NOT OCCUR UNTIL AFTER MORE SUBSTANTIAL CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING OCCURS WITHIN THE ONGOING WARM SECTOR. THIS BREEDS UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE OVERALL ORGANIZATION OF CONVECTION AND CORRESPONDING C

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS MAY PRODUCE STRONG WIND GUSTS THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON...THOUGH THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG INSOLATION/DIABATIC SFC HEATING AMIDST RICH DEEP MOISTURE OVER CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PARTS OF THE FL PENINSULA -- I.E. PW VALUES AROUND 1.7-1.9 INCHES PER GPS DATA -- IS FOSTERING MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-3000 J/KG PER MODIFIED 12Z MFL/TBW RAOBS. THE LARGE BUOYANCY IN MANY AREAS IS BEING FURTHER AIDED BY RELATIVELY LOW MID-LEVEL TEMPERATURES ACCOMPANYING A 500-MB THERMAL TROUGH -- I.E. 500-MB TEMPERATURES AROUND -8.5 TO -9C PER THE 12Z RAOBS. LOW-LEVEL ASCENT SUPPORTING INCREASING THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE/INTENSITY IS BEING BOLSTERED BY /1/ E AND W COAST SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS.../2/ DIURNALLY DEEPENING PLANETARY BOUNDARY LAYER CIRCULATIONS...AND /3/ DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONES OVER THE FRINGES OF MULTI-LAYERED CLOUDINESS ACCOMPANYING CONVECTION OVER THE COASTAL/OFFSHORE WATERS OFF THE SWRN FL PENINSULA/LOWER KEYS COASTS. THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY BECOME WIDESPREAD THROUGH THE AFTERNOON...AND SHOULD EVENTUALLY BECOME CONCENTRATED TOWARD THE W COAST BY LATE THIS AFTERNOON -- OWING TO A VERY MODEST ELY FLOW COMPONENT IN THE LOW LEVELS SAMPLED BY VWP/S OVER THE SWRN FRINGES OF A SWRN-N-ATLANTIC ANTICYCLONE. STRONG UPWARD MASS FLUXES ACCOMPANYING THE AFOREMENTIONED BUOYANCY AND STRONG PRECIP LOADING OWING TO THE HIGH PW MAY SUPPORT INTENSE WET MICROBURSTS IN THIS PULSE-TYPE CONVECTIVE ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY VERY WEAK DEEP SHEAR. A LOCALIZED DMGG WIND GUST CANNOT BE RULED OUT WHERE COLD POOLS LOCALLY MERGE/CONGLOMERATE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR POTENTIAL MAY BE INCREASING OVER DISCUSSION AREA AS LOW-LEVEL DESTABILIZATION CONTINUES...AMIDST RICH MOISTURE BUT WEAK LOW-LEVEL FLOW AND VARIABLE DEEP SHEAR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWS WELL-DEFINED CONVERGENCE/CONFLUENCE LINE...COLLOCATED WITH SFC TROUGH AND OBJECTIVELY ANALYZED VORTICITY AXIS...FROM NEAR DLH SSWWD INTO CENTRAL IA...AND MOVING SLOWLY EWD. THIS ALSO CORRESPONDS CLOSELY TO THETAE AXIS THAT EXTENDS FARTHER SWD...OVER NWRN MO. INITIALLY LOOSELY ORGANIZED AND BKN BELT OF CONVECTION HAS FORMED ALONG THAT BOUNDARY FROM PORTIONS DOUGLAS/BAYFIELD COUNTIES WI SSWWD ACROSS ERN FRINGES MSP METRO AREA AND ADJOINING PARTS OF EXTREME WRN WI. ADDITIONAL CONVECTION MAY DEVELOP/BACKBUILD BETWEEN THERE AND NRN IA...WITH LOWER PROBABILITY OF FILLING IN OVER NERN IA TOWARD ISOLATED CENTRAL IA TSTMS. PROXIMAL BOUNDARY LAYER IS ESSENTIALLY UNCAPPED EVEN FOR WEAK LIFT...NOW THAT CLOUD COVER FROM MORNING CONVECTION HAS DISPERSED AND PRECONVECTIVE SFC TEMPS HAVE RISEN INTO 80S F. SFC DEW POINTS LOW-MID 70S CONTRIBUTE TO MLCAPE 2000-2500 J/KG...LOCALLY 3000 J/KG...IN MODIFIED RAOBS AND FCST SOUNDINGS. DEEP SHEAR MOSTLY IS WEAK EXCEPT FOR PORTIONS SRN MN AND NRN IA...WHERE 40-50 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES ARE NOTED. THAT ENHANCED FLOW ALOFT IS RELATED TO MID-UPPER LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH PASSING OVER THIS REGION...PER MOISTURE CHANNEL IMAGERY...VWP AND WDL PROFILER TRENDS. ORGANIZATION OF NRN PARTS OF THIS ACTIVITY MAY BE LIMITED BY LACK OF MORE ROBUST DEEP SHEAR...WHILE RECOVERY OF AIR MASS IS TAKING LONGER OVER NERN/ERN IA AREA. HOWEVER...IF STORM-SCALE TRENDS INDICATE POTENTIAL FOR SUBSTANTIAL COLD-POOL DEVELOPMENT AND RESULTANT ENHANCEMENT TO BOTH FORCED ASCENT AND WIND-DAMAGE RISK...WW MAY BE REQUIRED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THERE WILL EXIST AN ISOLATED POTENTIAL FOR SVR THUNDERSTORMS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON...THOUGH THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MODERATE TO STRONG DESTABILIZATION IS UNDERWAY FROM PARTS OF THE SRN APPALACHIANS EWD TO THE ATLANTIC COAST...AS APPRECIABLE INSOLATION IS RESPONSIBLE FOR DIABATIC HEATING OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER AMIDST RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE -- I.E. SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S AND LOWER 70S. THIS IS SUPPORTING MLCAPE VALUES OF AROUND 1500-2500 J/KG PER MODIFIED 12Z RAOBS. THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY ACROSS THE MCD AREA PARTLY OWING TO LOW-LEVEL ASCENT FOCUSED INVOF THE FOLLOWING FEATURES: /1/ TERRAIN-DRIVEN CIRCULATIONS AROUND THE APPALACHIANS... /2/ SEA BREEZE CONVERGENCE ZONES ALONG THE ATLANTIC COASTAL PLAIN REGION... /3/ THE LEADING EDGE OF OUTFLOW ASSOCIATED WITH A NNE/SSW-ORIENTED...DISORGANIZED LINE OF CONVECTION APPROACHING FAR ERN TN FROM THE W... /4/ RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM CONVECTION ACROSS CNTRL SC... /5/ STRENGTHENING PLANETARY BOUNDARY LAYER CIRCULATIONS AMIDST A NEARLY UNCAPPED THERMODYNAMIC PROFILE. GENERALLY WEAK DEEP SHEAR ACROSS A LARGE PART OF THE AREA WILL FOSTER LIMITED CONVECTIVE ORGANIZATION/SUSTENANCE...THOUGH ISOLATED INSTANCES OF DMGG WIND GUSTS AND POSSIBLY MARGINALLY SVR HAIL CANNOT BE RULED OUT WITH THE MOST INTENSE STORMS OWING TO THE LARGE AMOUNT OF BUOYANCY. HOWEVER...AREA VWP DATA INDICATE AROUND 20 TO LOCALLY 25 KT OF WSWLY TO WNWLY MID-LEVEL FLOW IN THE BASE OF A WEAK MID-LEVEL TROUGH...WHICH COULD SUPPORT SUFFICIENT 0-6-KM BULK SHEAR FOR A COUPLE OF LOOSELY ORGANIZED MULTICELL CLUSTERS. ENSUING STRONGER/MERGING COLD POOLS MAY YIELD LOCALIZED AREAS OF STRONGER OUTFLOW WINDS...AIDED BY WATER LOADING PROCESSES WITH PW VALUES OF 1.5 TO 1.9 INCHES.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR INCREASING SVR POTENTIAL AND THE POSSIBLE ISSUANCE OF A SVR THUNDERSTORM WATCH THIS AFTERNOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ACROSS THE MCD AREA...A POCKET OF PARTLY CLOUDY TO MOSTLY SUNNY SKIES LIES BETWEEN HIGHER-DENSITY/OPAQUE MULTI-LAYERED CLOUDS STREAMING ACROSS CNTRL/NRN NEW ENGLAND...AND AN EWD-EXTENDING PLUME OF SIMILAR CLOUDS MOVING ESEWD ACROSS SERN NY AND SRN CT INTO THE ADJACENT WRN ATLANTIC. SFC DIABATIC HEATING ACROSS THIS POCKET OF ENHANCED ISOLATION AMIDST MIDDLE 60S SFC DEWPOINTS IS CONTRIBUTING TO AROUND 1000-1500 J/KG OF MLCAPE PER MODIFIED 12Z RAOBS AND FORECAST SOUNDINGS. FURTHER DESTABILIZATION WILL BE CONTRIBUTED BY /1/ CONTINUED STEEPENING OF LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES THROUGH THE AFTERNOON...AND /2/ INCREASING LARGE-SCALE UPWARD MOTION PRECEDING A MID-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH APPROACHING FROM THE GREAT LAKES REGION. THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY INCREASE IN NUMBER/INTENSITY THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AMIDST THE MODERATE INSTABILITY AS LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG THE FRINGES OF THE MULTI-LAYERED CLOUDS/DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONES IS AUGMENTED BY INLAND-MOVING SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS. BOX VWP DATA INDICATE AROUND 30 KT OF FLOW IN THE 3-5-KM-AGL LAYER...AND SOME INCREASE IN MID-LEVEL FLOW MAY OCCUR AS THE HEIGHT GRADIENT TIGHTENS IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE APPROACH OF THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH. CORRESPONDING MODERATE DEEP SHEAR MAY SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES INCLUDING MULTICELLS AND PERHAPS MARGINAL SUPERCELL STRUCTURES...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR DMGG WINDS AND SVR HAIL. HOWEVER...MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE NOT PARTICULARLY STEEP...AND THE STRONGEST DEEP-LAYER FORCING FOR ASCENT COULD REMAIN DISPLACED TO THE W OF THE AREA THROUGH PEAK HEATING. THESE FACTORS BREED UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE ANTICIPATED CONVECTIVE INTENSITY...THOUGH THE AREA WILL BE MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBLE ISSUANCE OF A SVR THUNDERSTORM WATCH THROUGH THE AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONTINUE WWS. SVR POTENTIAL -- PRIMARILY IN FORM OF DAMAGING WIND -- CONTINUES TO INCREASE WITH PRIMARY TSTM CLUSTER...MOVING ESEWD 35-40 KT WITH SOME LOCALIZED ACCELERATIONS OVER SRN INDIANA ATTM. INCREASINGLY ORGANIZED WIND THREAT IS APPARENT...ESPECIALLY ALONG AND JUST N OF SDF-LEX CORRIDOR...ESEWD INTO NERN KY. IN ADDITION A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT -- EITHER WITH LEADING-EDGE MISOVORTICES OR BURIED IN RAIN-WRAPPED BOOKEND CIRCULATIONS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: COLD POOL WITH THIS COMPLEX IS GROWING AND GETTING BETTER ORGANIZED. BOTH BOWING STRUCTURE AND REAR-INFLOW JET HAVE BECOME EVIDENT IN REFLECTIVITY/VELOCITY ANIMATIONS RESPECTIVELY...FROM IND AND LVX RADARS. 58 KT GUST WAS REPORTED IN LAWRENCE COUNTY INDIANA AT 1856Z. FOR ANOTHER 2-3 HOURS AT LEAST...TRACK OF MCS SHOULD REMAIN ASTRIDE RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ANALYZED FROM WRN-MOST WV IN BROAD WWD ARC ACROSS NRN KY. AIR MASS NOW IS FAVORABLY MOIST AND UNSTABLE ON BOTH SIDES OF THAT BOUNDARY. THIS IS EVIDENT IN PRECURSORY TSTMS DEVELOPING WITHIN LITTLE OR NO MLCINH...AND ONLY GRADUAL NEWD DROPOFF IN 2000-2500 WARM-SECTOR MLCAPE. OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...THOUGH DIFFUSE...SHOULD CONTINUE TO FOCUS BOUNDARY-LAYER VORTICITY AND AT LEAST SUBTLE LIFT. BULK OF ACTIVITY ALSO IS MOVING ASTRIDE AXIS OF CHANNEL OF MARGINAL...BUT RELATIVELY MAXIMIZED...DEEP SHEAR VECTORS THAT ARE NEARLY PARALLEL TO ORIENTATION OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND 30-35 KT IN MAGNITUDE. TRAILING CONVECTION OVER IL MAY POSE ISOLATED HAIL THREAT ON EITHER WIDE OF FRESH OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM MAIN MCS...AND DAMAGING WIND ALONG AND TO ITS S ACROSS MORE OF KY. ..EDWARDS.. 06/26/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR ISOLATED SVR THUNDERSTORMS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. WHILE CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED...THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS CURRENTLY UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ON THE HEELS OF WEAK MID-LEVEL SUBSIDENCE SUCCEEDING A SHORTWAVE TROUGH ENTERING ERN NY AND CNTRL NEW ENGLAND...INCREASING DCVA PRECEDING A PAIR OF MID-LEVEL IMPULSES CROSSING PARTS OF ERN ONTARIO AND WRN QUEBEC WILL GLANCE THE AREA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. ASSOCIATED MODEST DESTABILIZATION AND ENHANCED MID-LEVEL FLOW WILL MAINTAIN AN ENVIRONMENT CONDUCIVE FOR A FEW ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTERS. THUNDERSTORMS ARE STRENGTHENING ALONG A WSW/ENE-ORIENTED WEAK SFC STATIONARY FRONT ANALYZED FROM SERN ONTARIO AND INTO FAR SRN QUEBEC. THIS ACTIVITY MAY CROSS THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER AND AFFECT AREAS IN UPSTATE NY AROUND THE ADIRONDACK MOUNTAINS DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. SUCH CONVECTION WOULD LIKELY OFFER THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE SVR POTENTIAL ACROSS THE MCD AREA. ADDITIONAL CONVECTION DEVELOPING ALONG A LAKE ONTARIO SEA BREEZE BOUNDARY MAY ALSO STRENGTHEN AS IT CROSSES PARTS OF CNTRL NY INCLUDING THE FINGER LAKES REGION. MEANWHILE...LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG A DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ZONE ARCING FROM NRN VT INTO CNTRL/SWRN NY MAY ALSO FOCUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT. STRONGER INSOLATION W/N OF THIS ZONE IS SUPPORTING MLCAPE VALUES OF AROUND 1000-1500 J/KG. STORMS THIS AFTERNOON WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING STRONG WIND GUSTS...AND SPORADIC DMGG WINDS AND PERHAPS MARGINALLY SVR HAIL CANNOT BE RULED OUT WITH THE MOST INTENSE STORM CLUSTERS/UPDRAFTS. HOWEVER...WITH AN OVERALL DECREASING TREND IN PW VALUES PER GPS DATA...UPDRAFT MASS FLUXES/CONVECTIVE VIGOR MAY BE SUPPRESSED TO SOME EXTENT. FURTHERMORE...DEEP-LAYER FORCING FOR ASCENT IS NOT EXPECTED TO BE ESPECIALLY STRONG...WHICH MAY ONLY BE ASSOCIATED WITH AN ISOLATED SVR POTENTIAL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED SVR STORMS WILL EXIST THROUGH THE AFTERNOON HOURS. WHILE CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED...THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS CURRENTLY UNLIKELY.

HOWEVER...IN THE ABSENCE OF STRONGER BUOYANCY OWING TO LIMITED LOW/MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...CONVECTIVE VIGOR AND SVR POTENTIAL MAY BE LIMITED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SPORADIC SVR HAIL AND DAMAGING GUSTS MAY OCCUR WITH CONVECTION MOVING ESEWD ACROSS DAKOTAS AND PARTS OF SWRN MN. THREAT APPEARS TOO DISORGANIZED AND ISOLATED FOR WW ATTM.

DESPITE THAT VEERING...HOWEVER...STG MID-UPPER WINDS CONTRIBUTE TO FAVORABLE DEEP SHEAR...WITH EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES 40-50 KT ACROSS MUCH OF THIS AREA. EXPERIMENTAL VERSION-2 OF RR MODEL APPEARS TO BE DEPICTING THAT MIXED LAYER MORE REPRESENTATIVELY THAN ORIGINAL RR...AND ADJUSTED SOUNDINGS YIELD 1000-1500 J/KG MLCAPE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR SVR STORMS CONTINUES ACROSS SVR THUNDERSTORM WATCH 373.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS ADVANCING FROM THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS TO THE PIEDMONT REGION WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A THREAT FOR DMGG WIND GUSTS AND POSSIBLY MARGINALLY SVR HAIL AS THEY ENCOUNTER STRONG INSTABILITY DOWNSTREAM. WHERE CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING HAS NOT YET OCCURRED...THE PRESENCE OF LITTLE SUBSTANTIVE CINH AND MLCAPE AROUND 2000-3000 J/KG PER MODIFIED 12Z RAOBS WILL SUPPORT INTENSE UPDRAFTS/DOWNDRAFTS. AND...WITH STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES YIELDING DCAPE IN EXCESS OF 1000 J/KG...STRONG DOWNDRAFTS/DMGG WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE -- PARTICULARLY WITH ANY CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS THAT EVOLVE. MARGINALLY SVR HAIL WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE. THE PRESENCE OF AROUND 20-30 KT OF QUASI-ZONAL MID-LEVEL FLOW PER FCX/LWX VWP DATA WILL ALLOW FORWARD PROPAGATION OF ONGOING CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS...WITH PARTS OF CNTRL/S-CNTRL VA MOST SUSCEPTIBLE TO EXPERIENCING THIS ACTIVITY IN THE NEAR TERM. HOWEVER...ADDITIONAL SVR STORM DEVELOPMENT REMAINS POSSIBLE FARTHER NE INTO PARTS OF SERN PA AND SRN NJ WHERE CONVECTION IS BLOSSOMING FROM A DEEPENING CUMULUS INLAND. ..COHEN.. 06/26/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS ACROSS THIS AREA MAY PRODUCE OCNL STG-SVR GUSTS AND MRGL HAIL...INCLUDING PORTIONS STL METRO AREA...BEFORE MOVING SEWD INTO WW 372. SW OF THAT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...AND ESPECIALLY ALONG AND SW OF DIFFERENTIAL-HEATING ZONE...BOUNDARY-LAYER AIR MASS HAS BECOME MINIMALLY INHIBITED AND FAVORABLY BUOYANT...WITH SFC DEW POINTS COMMONLY 70S F CONTRIBUTING TO MLCAPE 2000-3000 J/KG. STRENGTHENING BELT OF NWLYS ALOFT IS ALIGNED PARALLEL TO THOSE BOUNDARIES AND ENHANCED SOMEWHAT SW OF AN MCV OVER EXTREME SERN WI. THIS CONTRIBUTES TO 40-50 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR VECTORS ALSO ORIENTED MOSTLY ALONG THOSE BOUNDARIES. THOUGH LOW-LEVEL SRH IS WEAK...BASED ON VWP AND FCST SOUNDINGS...SUCH DEEP SHEAR MAY SUPPORT AT LEAST TRANSIENT SUPERCELLULAR CHARACTERISTICS IN SUPPORT OF WIND/HAIL POTENTIAL.

mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CUMULUS HAVE BECOME MORE AGITATED ALONG THE DRYLINE ACROSS WRN TX LATE THIS AFTERNOON. HIGH-RES MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT A FEW STORMS MAY DEVELOP ALONG THE DRYLINE NORTH OF ONGOING CONVECTION IN THE TX BIG BEND AREA. WEAK DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL LIMIT LONGEVITY/ORGANIZATION OF ANY FURTHER STORMS THAT DEVELOP. BUT...STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE AROUND 2500 J PER KG/ IN A WEAKLY CAPPED ENVIRONMENT IN THE VICINITY OF THE DRYLINE WILL SUPPORT THE POTENTIAL FOR AT LEAST AS SHORT-LIVED THREAT FOR ANY STORMS THAT DO DEVELOP. STEEP LAPSE RATES AND DCAPE VALUES OVER 1500 J/KG WILL ALLOW FOR BOTH A HAIL AND STRONG WIND THREAT. STORMS MAY TRACK EWD OFF THE DRYLINE BUT ARE NOT EXPECTED TO MAKE IT VERY FAR BEFORE DIURNAL COOLING LEADS TO WEAKENING CONVECTION AFTER AROUND 00-02Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LINE OF CONVECTION WILL CONTINUE MOVING ACROSS CNTRL NC FOR A FEW MORE HOURS. AS THE LINE OF STORMS APPROACHES THE COASTAL PLAIN...WEAKENING IS EXPECTED. SPORADIC STRONG/DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL CONTINUE TO BE POSSIBLE UNTIL STORMS WEAKEN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF CONVECTION ACROSS CNTRL NC HAS MAINTAINED ORGANIZATION...MAINLY DUE TO COLD POOL DEVELOPMENT AND A MOIST/UNSTABLE DOWNSTREAM ENVIRONMENT. THIS LINE OF STORMS SHOULD CONTINUE FOR AT LEAST A COUPLE MORE HOURS AS IT MOVES ACROSS THE PIEDMONT. SPORADIC STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE INTO THE EVENING. AS THE STORMS TRACK EWD TOWARD THE COASTAL PLAIN...WEAKENING IS EXPECTED. ONGOING CONVECTION ACROSS THE COASTAL PLAIN HAS LEAD TO A COOLER AIRMASS WITH WEAKENING INSTABILITY WITH CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE COAST. WITH THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING...FURTHER STABILIZATION/CAPPING OF THE AIRMASS WILL OCCUR AND STORMS WILL WEAKEN/DIMINISH.

THE MOST SUSTAINED/CONCENTRATED SEVERE THREAT MAY EXIST OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS ACROSS FAR SOUTHERN IL/EXTREME SOUTHEAST MO AND WESTERN KY...AND PERHAPS EVENTUALLY INTO WESTERN TN.

VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN FAVORABLE FOR TRANSIENT SUPERCELLS NEAR/ATOP THE SURFACE COLD POOL...ALTHOUGH CONVECTIVE MODE/DEGREE OF UPSCALE GROWTH WILL HINDER THIS POTENTIAL. REGARDLESS...PERIODIC BOUTS OF SEVERE HAIL/LOCALIZED WIND DAMAGE WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THROUGH EARLY/MID EVENING FROM FAR SOUTHERN INDIANA INTO NORTH-CENTRAL KY. MEANWHILE...FARTHER WEST...A SURFACE-BASED CLUSTER OF STORMS /WITH PERIPHERAL TRANSIENT SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT POSSIBLE/ WILL LIKELY TO CONTINUE TO SPREAD SOUTHEASTWARD/POTENTIALLY GROW UPSCALE WITHIN A WARM/MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIRMASS /2000-3000 J PER KG MLCAPE/ ACROSS EXTREME SOUTHEAST MO/FAR SOUTHERN IL INTO WEST-CENTRAL KY. DAMAGING WINDS/BOUTS OF SEVERE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THROUGH EARLY EVENING ESPECIALLY IN AREAS BETWEEN I-55/I-57...WITH PERSISTENCE INTO WESTERN KY /AND PERHAPS EVENTUALLY WESTERN TN/ LIKELY. ..GUYER.. 06/26/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WITH A STRONG/SEVERE MCS LIKELY TO CONTINUE SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS WESTERN/CENTRAL/SOUTHEAST PORTIONS OF KY INTO TN THROUGH LATE EVENING...A NEW SEVERE TSTM WATCH AND/OR AN EXTENSION OF WATCH 372 ACROSS KY /SCHEDULED TO EXPIRE 03Z/ MAY BE NEEDED BEFORE 03Z/10 PM CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: FOCUSED ALONG PRIOR OUTFLOW...UPSCALE MCS GROWTH HAS OCCURRED ALONG THE OH RIVER NEAR THE INDIANA-KY BORDER...WITH SOME FORWARD/SOUTHEASTWARD ACCELERATION EVIDENT OVER THE PAST HOUR. CONTINUED SOUTHEASTWARD PERSISTENCE OF THESE POTENTIALLY CONSOLIDATING CLUSTERS WILL BE AIDED BY A MODERATELY STRONG BELT OF NORTHWESTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW AND/OR REAR INFLOW...WITH 35-40 KT BETWEEN 3-6 KM NOW EVIDENT IN WSR-88D VWP DATA FROM PADUCAH/EVANSVILLE. GIVEN THIS BACKGROUND FLOW AND EXISTING QUASI-LINEAR ORGANIZATION...WIND DAMAGE/SEVERE HAIL POTENTIAL SHOULD CONTINUE SOUTHEASTWARD BEYOND THE 03Z TIME FRAME...ALTHOUGH GRADUAL BOUNDARY LAYER COOLING MAY BEGIN TO TEMPER THE WIND DAMAGE LIKELIHOOD INTO LATE EVENING/OVERNIGHT. EVEN SO...AN ADDITIONAL SEVERE TSTM WATCH AND/OR TEMPORAL EXTENSION OF WW 372 MAY BE NEEDED.

A 46 KT GUST WAS MEASURED AT SOMERSET KY AS OF 0415Z. WHILE CLOUD TOPS HAVE BEGUN TO WARM PER IR SATELLITE IMAGERY AND THE INTEGRITY OF THE CONVECTIVE LINE/LEADING UPLIFT HAS TENDED TO DIMINISH...LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS WILL NONETHELESS REMAIN POSSIBLE DURING THE FIRST PART OF THE OVERNIGHT FROM FAR SOUTHEAST KY INTO EASTERN TN AND PERHAPS FAR WESTERN PORTIONS OF VA/NC GIVEN THE FORWARD MOTION OF THE MCS/COLD POOL. MEANWHILE...A WESTERN FRAGMENT OF THE MCS/COLD POOL WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE SOUTH-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS WEST-CENTRAL TN AND PERHAPS REACH NORTHERN AL. THIS PORTION OF THE LINE HAS ACCESS TO A GREATER RESERVOIR OF INSTABILITY /1000+ J PER KG MLCAPE/...REFLECTED AT THE SURFACE WITH TEMPERATURES REMAINING IN THE LOWER 80S F AS OF 04Z. DAMAGING WINDS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE ON A LOCALIZED BASIS...WITH SEVERE HAIL ALSO A POSSIBILITY ON THE WESTERN FLANK OF THIS ACTIVITY. ..GUYER.. 06/27/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTM COVERAGE IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE OVER THE NEXT COUPLE HRS ACROSS CNTRL AND NERN NEB ALONG THE NOSE OF A LLJ...AND COULD EXPAND E-SEWD WITH TIME. THE ENVIRONMENT WILL BE SUPPORTIVE FOR ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS A FEW STRONG-SVR WIND GUSTS. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR MOSAIC LOOP SHOWS INCREASING ELEVATED TSTMS ACROSS NERN AND CNTRL NEB WITHIN THE PAST 1-2 HRS...FORMING WITHIN A WAA REGIME ORIENTED ENE-WSW ALONG THE NOSE OF A 30-40 KT LLJ /AS SAMPLED BY LNX VWP DATA/. STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WITHIN A MOIST AIR MASS ARE YIELDING MUCAPE VALUES ABOVE 1500 J/KG. THIS...ALONG WITH MODERATELY STRONG BULK SHEAR WITHIN THE CLOUD-BEARING LAYER...WILL SUPPORT THE POTENTIAL FOR SOME ORGANIZED CONVECTION CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL. DESPITE THIS ACTIVITY LIKELY BEING ELEVATED...MODIFIED 27/00Z OBSERVED AND MODEL FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THE DEPTH OF THE NEAR-SFC STABLE LAYER IS SHALLOW...AND COULD SUPPORT STRONG TO POSSIBLY SVR WIND GUSTS IF A COLD POOL CAN MATERIALIZE. CURRENT THINKING IS THAT TSTMS WILL CONTINUE TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE/INTENSITY OVER THE NEXT 2-3 HRS AND EVENTUALLY SPREAD E-SEWD INTO ERN NEB...NERN KS...AND POSSIBLY FAR WRN IA. THE POTENTIAL FOR A WW WILL BE DEPENDENT ON INDICATIONS OF AN ORGANIZED WIND/HAIL THREAT DEVELOPING...AND TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED FOR THIS POSSIBILITY.
